newsitem.title: LIBYA: Rwanda calls for three-sided talks in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda calls for three-sided talks in Zaire.

text.p: Rwandan Foreign Minister Anastase Gasana has welcomed a drive by South African President Nelson Mandela to find a political solution to the conflict in Zaire.

"We support President Mandela's efforts between the regime of Mobutu and Mr. Kabila...It seems that these talks were going on well," Anastase Gasana told Reuters on Wednesday night in the Libyan capital Tripoli where he was attending an Organisation of African Unity conference.
Mandela met Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Wednesday and held talks with a special envoy of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on Thursday to accelerate moves to peace talks for Zaire.
The Rwandan minister said any direct talks between rebels and the government in Zaire must be three-sided to include the main Zairean political opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi.

"We think that we must act to have Mr. Kabila and his armed opposition, Mr. Tshisekedi and his political opposition, and Mr. Mobutu and his government sit around a table to find a political solution to the problems of the country," Gasana said.
Zaire says rebels who hold a large swathe of territory in eastern Zaire were backed by soldiers from Burundi, Rwanda and Uganda. All three countries deny the charge.
